WodeMac · Remote Mac guides

Control a remote Mac mini from your phone, iPad or computer

Reviewed: 2026-11-21 · WodeMac

One cloud Mac can be reached from a phone, an iPad and a computer. It is delivered with WodeMac Remote Screen: phones and iPads open the remote desktop in a browser, and computers use the WodeMac Mac app or a browser. Builds, tests and scripts run on the Mac in California, so switching devices or losing the connection only drops the picture and does not stop the work.

What each device is good for

  • Phone: open the remote desktop in a browser to check build and test progress, read logs and make quick confirmations on the go.
  • iPad: open the remote desktop in a browser to review results and interfaces, make light edits with a keyboard, or demo in a meeting.
  • Computer: use the WodeMac Mac app or a browser for the full desktop, long development sessions, Xcode and debugging.

All three reach the same Mac and the same desktop, so you can stop on one device and pick up on another.

Why switching devices does not interrupt work

Builds, tests and scripts run on the Mac in California; the device in your hand only shows the picture and passes along keyboard, mouse or touch input. Closing the phone browser, shutting a laptop or changing Wi-Fi drops that display link and nothing else. Reconnect and you are back at the same desktop with the same windows.

For long jobs, use tmux or run them under launchd with a log file. Then the job continues even if a terminal window is closed, and the output is there to read from any device.

Checking progress from a phone

  • Open the remote desktop and look at the terminal window or the Xcode build result.
  • Have jobs write to a log file and read the latest lines with tail -n 50 ~/logs/build.log, which is easier than scrolling windows on a small screen.
  • If you have turned on SSH (Remote Login) yourself and confirmed it is reachable, connect with an SSH client app on your phone and run tmux attach to rejoin a running session.
  • Have scripts send an email or a message to your team chat when they finish, so your phone tells you when to look.

Practical tips

  • On a phone, stick to checking and small actions; switch to a computer or an iPad with a keyboard for real typing.
  • Do not save connection passwords on shared devices, and sign in separately on each device.
  • Responsiveness depends on your network path to California; on a weak mobile connection, rely on logs and the command line.
  • Each Mac is rented to one customer. For people working in parallel over a long period, one Mac each avoids competing for the same desktop.

FAQ

Can an iPad be my main device for a remote Mac?

You can open the full remote desktop in a browser and, with a keyboard, do light development and reviews comfortably. For long coding sessions and Xcode work, a computer is still better.

Does a running job stop if my phone loses signal?

No. The job runs on the Mac in California and the phone is only a window for viewing and input. Reconnecting returns you to the same desktop.

Do I need a dedicated app on my phone?

A browser is enough for the remote desktop. If you have turned on SSH yourself, you can also use any SSH client app.

Can several people connect to one Mac at once?

Each Mac is rented to one customer, and how a team shares it is up to you. The remote screen shows one desktop, so people working at the same time get in each other's way; for long-term parallel work, one Mac each is better.
